what_it_does: Fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) on a new task normally requires storing and updating billions of numbers, which is impractical on small devices. DuQTTA combines two compression ideas: Tensor-Train decomposition, which breaks each giant weight matrix into a chain of much smaller matrices whose product approximates the original, and dual-stage quantization, which stores those smaller matrices using fewer bits (reducing file size and memory footprint further). An additional trick separates how big a weight's magnitude is from the direction it points, updating each independently so the compressed model stays accurate. The paper reports up to 65x compression on the LLaMA2-7B model while outperforming a popular baseline called LoRA, making fine-tuning feasible on edge hardware — though these claims come from the abstract alone.
